title: Make unknown-SKU errors point at their caller

blocks.text: The cart, the search page and the order service all ask the catalog for prices, and unknown SKUs are frequent: old links, typos, a search that tries SKUs as the user types. Two complaints reached the team last week. The order service started sending a SKU that never existed, and the error log, which records each failure with its stack trace, pointed at the search page, which had asked for that SKU first, that morning. And the search page, which calls `find(...)` on every keystroke, spends most of its CPU on SKUs that don't exist.

items: `unknown(...)`: the exception `price(...)` throws for a SKU the catalog doesn't sell. It names the SKU, and its trace shows the code that asked, even when another caller asked for the same SKU before or after.
`find(...)`: the price, or nothing, for the search page.

cases.says: a known SKU gets its price, and an unknown one fails with UnknownSkuException naming the SKU, whose trace shows the caller
find gives the price of a known SKU and nothing for an unknown one
when a second caller asks for the same unknown SKU, its exception's trace shows that second caller
an exception already handed to one caller keeps that caller in its trace after another caller asks for the same SKU
looking up unknown SKUs with find builds no exception

origin.section: The Stack Trace Is Recorded Where the Exception Is Created, Not Where It Is Thrown

concepts: A throw costs microseconds, mostly for filling in the stack trace, so an expected outcome on a hot path is better returned than thrown.
The stack trace is recorded when the exception is created, so a shared instance reports where it was made, and refilling it rewrites the trace of failures already handed out.
